title: App And Desktop Migration Boundary
objective: Create the app-side and desktop-side migration seams that let the product opt into Server V2 without scattering transport or startup logic across unrelated call sites.

steps.name: Define the logical rollout flag contract
steps.description: Choose the single logical flag name and expected behavior for legacy mode versus Server V2 mode so the app and desktop shell share one rollout decision.
successFactors: There is one logical flag for both UI routing and desktop startup.
Flag semantics match `ui-migration.md`.
The chosen naming is recorded clearly for later phases and tests.

steps.name: Add the shared UI rollout helper
steps.description: Implement a single app-side helper such as `checkServerFlag()` or `isServerV2Enabled()` that hides env details from feature code.
successFactors: App call sites use one shared helper instead of reading env vars directly.
The helper returns a simple boolean and is easy to reuse.
The helper lives in a clear shell or kernel location.

steps.name: Bridge the rollout flag into desktop startup
steps.description: Ensure the desktop/native layer can see the same logical flag and make the same startup decision without inventing a second product switch.
successFactors: Tauri startup follows the same logical flag as the frontend.
Platform-specific env handling is hidden behind one implementation boundary.
There is no separate hidden desktop-only rollout toggle.

steps.name: Add app-side `createSdk({ serverId })`
steps.description: Create the app-owned runtime adapter that prepares the generated SDK for a given server target and becomes the stable entrypoint for Server V2 calls.
successFactors: Feature code can call `createSdk({ serverId })` instead of passing raw URLs around.
The adapter remains thin and transport-focused.
The generated SDK package stays server-agnostic and reusable.

steps.name: Implement server target resolution
steps.description: Resolve `serverId` into base URL, token, hosting metadata, and capabilities from the app's current server records without forcing feature code to understand connection details.
successFactors: The adapter can construct a typed client from `serverId`.
Feature code does not pass `baseUrl` and `token` manually.
The implementation is cheap enough for per-call client creation.

steps.name: Inject auth and capability handling in the adapter
steps.description: Teach the adapter to attach auth headers and look at target capabilities so migration logic stays at the transport boundary rather than leaking into product code.
successFactors: Auth header injection is centralized.
Capability checks are possible without extra feature-level plumbing.
The adapter remains lightweight and does not become a second app runtime engine.

steps.name: Create a quarantined legacy shim area
steps.description: Add an app-local place for remaining legacy route helpers so call sites can branch cleanly during migration without preserving the old transport everywhere.
successFactors: Legacy compatibility helpers live in one obvious area.
The generated SDK package does not mix old and new contracts together.
Legacy helpers are thin enough to delete quickly once migrated.

steps.name: Add response normalization at the migration boundary
steps.description: Normalize old and new response shapes close to the adapter or shim boundary so the rest of the UI can consume stable app-facing data during rollout.
successFactors: Feature code does not branch on legacy versus Server V2 payload shape.
Normalization stays close to the transport layer.
The approach covers the payload categories called out in `ui-migration.md`.

steps.name: Add migration routing helpers
steps.description: Provide shared helpers for deciding whether a capability should use the legacy path or the Server V2 path, based on the rollout flag, target capabilities, and temporary rollout rules.
successFactors: Migration branching logic is reusable and easy to remove later.
Feature code can branch with minimal boilerplate.
The helpers support per-feature or per-endpoint migration.

steps.name: Add request-path observability during rollout
steps.description: Implement simple logging or telemetry that shows whether a migrated call used the legacy path or the Server V2 path so rollout debugging is practical.
successFactors: Developers can tell which backend path was used for a request.
The signal is available in dev without deep manual tracing.
The instrumentation does not leak into rendering code.

steps.name: Add the desktop startup branch
steps.description: Teach the Tauri startup boundary to choose between the legacy local runtime startup path and launching Server V2 directly based on the shared rollout flag.
successFactors: Flag-off preserves current behavior.
Flag-on launches Server V2 instead of assembling the old local stack where feasible.
The startup branch lives in one native location rather than many commands.

steps.name: Add the native Server V2 launch path
steps.description: Implement the native launch wiring needed for desktop mode to start the new server binary or dev process and retain minimal connection state for the app.
successFactors: The desktop shell can launch Server V2 reliably.
Minimal reconnect information is persisted or passed forward cleanly.
The shell does not resume ownership of workspace behavior just to launch the server.

steps.name: Align app boot with the new boundary
steps.description: Update app boot code so status probes, connection setup, and startup routing flow through the shared helper and adapter instead of ad hoc local assumptions.
successFactors: Startup code no longer bypasses the migration seam.
Flag-on and flag-off startup both use explicit boundaries.
The app boot path becomes easier for later phases to migrate slice by slice.

steps.name: Migrate initial system health/status probes
steps.description: Move the first low-risk probe paths, such as health and status checks, onto `createSdk({ serverId })` so the new boundary gets real usage before feature-heavy slices begin.
successFactors: The app can fetch basic server health through the new adapter.
Legacy fallback still works when the flag is off.
The first migrated calls are easy to verify end to end.

steps.name: Mark feature-level migration boundaries
steps.description: Identify and update the next feature call sites that should branch through the shared helper so later phases have known integration points instead of rediscovering them.
successFactors: The next migration slices have obvious branch points.
Raw env parsing is not scattered into new feature code.
The codebase shows a consistent migration pattern.

steps.name: Test flag-off behavior
steps.description: Add tests or smoke coverage proving that legacy mode still works after the migration boundary is added.
successFactors: Legacy boot and request routing remain functional.
The rollout boundary does not break the default path.
Regression checks exist for future boundary edits.

steps.name: Test flag-on behavior
steps.description: Add tests or smoke coverage proving that enabling the rollout flag launches Server V2 and routes migrated calls through the new adapter correctly.
successFactors: Server V2 mode is testable, not only a manual hidden mode.
The startup branch and transport branch agree with each other.
Developers can tell if Server V2 mode regresses before broader rollout.

steps.name: Record rollout caveats and cleanup rules
steps.description: Document any temporary branch behavior, escape hatches, or known cleanup triggers in learnings or open questions so compatibility code does not fossilize silently.
successFactors: Temporary migration branches have visible deletion criteria.
Known rollout caveats are written down for later phases.
Phase 4 leaves a clean seam rather than a second permanent architecture.
